pr_title: Improve SmartThings stale refresh token handling
pr_body:
## Breaking change

## Proposed change
Improves handling of when the SmartThings refresh token is stale/invalid:
- No longer removes the config entry and instead fails entry setup
- Creates a notification with a link and instructions to reauthorize the SmartApp
- Recovers (reloads the config entry) when the user reauthorizes, which sends a new refresh token to HA


## Type of change
- [X] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [X] New feature (which adds functionality to an existing integration)

## Additional information
- This PR fixes or closes issue: fixes #34102

There are two ways to reauthorize the SmartApp and recover the integration: Follow the link in the notification displayed in the frontend or through the SmartThings mobile application:
1. While HA is running, open the SmartThings mobile application and go into the SmartApps panel.
1. Click the Home Assistant (or whatever you named it) SmartApp
1. Click 'Done' then 'Allow'.  HA will update automatically.

Let me clarify a few things:
- If you are getting a HTTP 400 or 401 issue related to a refresh token, the only way to mitigate the issue is to completely remove the integration, [clean-up your ST account using this utility](https://pypi.org/project/hass-smartthings-remove/), and setup the integration from scratch.  Please wait 15 minutes before starting over again to give the caches time to reset.
- The refresh token gets out of sync if the HA process is not gracefully shutdown and there was a pending write.  Do not kill or force terminate the HA process.

Check your logs.  If you are experiencing other errors, it's a different issue.

I've been investigating this issue but haven't been able to reproduce it as described. The SmartThings integration obtains a new refresh token upon startup of HA and saves that in the config entry.  If the HA process is terminated or killed before the save is complete, the new token isn't persisted and the integration removes the config entry and asks you to reconfigure it (aka "deletes itself") the next time it starts up.  Outside that scenario, I haven't been able to reproduce the issue through a restart or upgrade and I've done this countless times through docker as well as a venv. I'm wondering if the following are possibly the issues, which would cause the problem:
1) You aren't persisting the configuration directory in Docker. When the container is restarted, the changes to the config entries (including the new token) are lost.  Solution: Ensure your configuration directory is a persisted/passed through volume.
2) You're overwriting the configuration directory on an upgrade with an older/previous version.  The new token is then lost.  Solution: Don't overwrite your configuration directory, or ensure it's backed up after the HA process has excited gracefully.

@danielgoepp A few corrections: The `401` occurs when trying to obtain the new access token / refresh token pair.  When a `401` is received at that step, there is no recovery path, as the integration no longer has a valid credential to use (retrying it won't fix anything), so it initiates a new config flow for the user to setup the integration again--which is the convention for integrations in HA when the auth is no longer valid.  The ST API works differently than other APIs in that access tokens have an extremely short TTL (5 min) and refresh tokens are single use only, so keys get rotated very frequently.

I personally run HA in a docker and do my development in a virtual environment and have ST setup in both.  This issue has never occurred for me and I restart HA very frequently--especially my venv.  There appears to be other factors/issues that cause the token to get out of sync.

review_comments: Would it be possible to start a new config flow instead with an external step?
No - the whole integration doesn't need to be setup again -- just this step to complete which sends a new `refresh token` to the webhook endpoint.

We can abort after that step is completed. It's not super smooth, but a persistent notification is even more not meant for this. We want to use the config flow to update the config when the user needs to do something.

I don't think that makes sense.  The config flow would require extensive changes as the external step is at the end.  We'd basically need an entirely new flow that has different steps, updates an existing entry, and aborts?  That's not a good user experience at all.  I don't see why we can't use a notification for this--it seems to be the optimal user experience.

The user experience would be the same. See the samsungtv integration for an example:

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/5bfc1f3d4d6e43bc02a127ac773d6cc45556bf03/homeassistant/components/samsungtv/media_player.py#L106-L113

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/5bfc1f3d4d6e43bc02a127ac773d6cc45556bf03/homeassistant/components/samsungtv/config_flow.py#L163-L176

I'm trying to implement this but here's what it's requiring:
- I need to version the config entries because ST isn't setting `unique_id`, which is needed for the config flow to replace an existing entry
- In the discovered entries, there isn't a way to specify a title (AFAIK) so all it says is "SmartThings" which isn't distinguishable if this happens to multiple locations at the same time.  Additionally the original integration is still there, which is very confusing and unclear what is wrong.  There's no clear call to action for the user to know they need to do something.
- At the completion of the flow, `async_remove_entry` is getting called on the old entry, which the ST integration was already using to clean up the ST account.  I now need to figure out how to introduce logic to not run this code if there's another in-flight entry.  This also breaks any custom named entries the user set for the integration.  

I don't think this is the right approach.  All I need to do is update a data attribute in an existing config entry and then reload it.  Removing the entry causes a loss of custom named entities.

This should indeed be done in a reauth with an external step. You can poll in the background if the user has clicked on allow. Note, you don't need to finish the flow with a create_entry. You can also update the existing entry and then abort it. That way you don't need to fight with `unload`. 

In 109 we're going to allow renaming config entries, so the titles should start making a bit more sense. 

For unique ID migration, we've been doing this: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/188f3e35fdab484f368fcb6c238fed8392022f57/homeassistant/components/hue/__init__.py#L125-L129

Oh and one more thing, you can specify a `flow_title` in your `strings.json/config` to specify a title with placeholders for a config flow. That way you know what it relates to: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/deconz/strings.json#L4
Thanks I'll look into those things.  If I abort at the end after updating the config entry, is the user shown an "Abort" window?
Yes, but you can control the translation text, so you just say: "Yo, auth updated, thank you! 🥂"
Isn't it normally that the refresh token is static, and you get new access tokens ?

In the ST API, the `refresh token` is single use and only valid for 30 days.  When you call the API for a new token, you get a `access token` and `refresh token` pair.

The integration stores the new refresh token during entry setup, but because the actual persistence is a background task, sometimes the token gets lost if the HA process isn't gracefully shutdown or crashes.  Seems to happen quite a bit to people in the wild.
Let's not make it a background task maybe ? If something takes 0.5 second longer (worst case), that's fine.
